metric_and_methodology_notes.gqa_vs_mla_attention_metric: In synthetic_fidelity_summary, gqa_standard (where V is present) computes simulated attention-weighted Value output cosine similarity cos(softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d))V, softmax(QK_hat^T/sqrt(d))V_hat), whereas single-buffer deepseek_mla (where V is None) computes softmax attention-weights cosine similarity cos(softmax(QK^T/sqrt(d)), softmax(QK_hat^T/sqrt(d))). Both are stored under py_attn_out_cos / cpp_attn_out_cos for schema uniformity and tagged via attn_metric_kind.
metric_and_methodology_notes.kv_and_query_rng_seeds: generate_realistic_kv_page always resets torch.manual_seed(42) on its target device, and evaluate_attention_fidelity always resets torch.manual_seed(99) on k_ref.device when sampling query q. Section 1 synthesizes the seed=42 KV page on device='mps' (when available) before copying to CPU (cpp_attn_out_cos=0.996103), whereas Section 4 synthesizes the seed=42 KV page directly on device='cpu' (cpp_attention_cosine_similarity=0.995925); there is no second independent KV seed=99 sample.
metric_and_methodology_notes.quantizer_precision_and_device_query_not: FusedColdPageCodec (Python) is mixed-precision (FP16 input/output tensors and FP16 stored group scales with FP32 intermediate group division). NativeCppFusedColdPageCodec (C++17 ARMv8.5-A NEON, csrc/fused_cold_page_cpu.cpp) computes FP16 group abs-max (vmaxvq_f16), widens to FP32 for scale and exact IEEE-754 reciprocal division (vectorized vdivq_f32 in 4-group kernels; scalar 1.0f / static_cast<float>(sc) in 2-group fallback), narrows the reciprocal to FP16 (vcvt_f16_f32 / vdupq_n_f16), and executes vectorized FP16 multiplication and nearest-even rounding (vmulq_f16, vcvtnq_s16_f16). Because Section 1 evaluates Python on MPS and C++ on CPU, query q (seed=99) is sampled from device-specific RNG streams.
metric_and_methodology_notes.tier_progression_and_buffer_scope: Speedup ratios (20.85x, 7.42x, 1.53x, 11.32x, 236.05x) are descriptive incremental implementation-tier comparisons across compounded changes (language/runtime, quantizer rounding, BLAKE2b vs. SipHash-2-4-128 MAC backend, batch size 1->64->256, threading runtime, and per-call allocation vs. caller-preallocated CPU uint8 tensor buffer), not controlled single-factor causal ablations isolating register fusion or NIC RDMA registration.
metric_and_methodology_notes.int4_cpu_rdma_speedup_estimator_note: rdma_100gbe_4k_prefix_64layers_model.ztcp_fused_int4_cpu_speedup_vs_raw_bf16=1.26 (std=0.01) is the mean of the 5 per-run 2-decimal rounded ratios [1.25, 1.27, 1.27, 1.24, 1.26], whereas the ratio of the 5-run mean latencies (95.87 ms / 76.28 ms = 1.2568x) rounds to 1.26x.
metric_and_methodology_notes.rdma_and_security_test_scope: Section 5 is an analytical serial-egress latency model combining measured M3 Max CPU compute time (or hypothetical 950 GB/s GPU SRAM compute time) with analytical 100GbE wire time at 11.2 GB/s. In the bundled benchmark (run_security_verification), tests 3.1-3.4 run on the Python reference codec (with 3.3 simulating a 1-bit flip in local memory), 3.5-3.9 and 3.11 run on the native C++17 Peak path + EphemeralSessionKeyRing, 3.10a-c exercises Native Peak duplicate-nonce and stale-replay checks plus the Python pack_chacha20_nonce helper, and 3.12 exercises Native Peak same-nonce race + Native Single failed-encode nonce burn and monotonic watermark checks. In-flight egress and ingress shred checks across all four codec paths (py_single, cpp_single, cpp_batch, cpp_peak) are verified in verify_package2.py, CODE-003; overlapping-batch checks are verified in B6-2.
